subject: SlateBridge billing migration to Azure Marketplace — economics & amendment
messages:
From: Sara Lim <procurement@slatebridge.com>

Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: SlateBridge billing migration to Azure Marketplace — impact & timelines

Hi Kimberly,

Quick intro — I'm Sara (procurement) at SlateBridge. We're coming up on our renewal and our finance team wants to move to Azure Marketplace billing to consolidate spend. Before we engage procurement formally, can you help clarify:

- High-level economics: any differences in list pricing vs our direct invoice today?
- How we handle existing committed discounts / credits if we move channels mid-term?
- Timing for a cutover (when would invoices begin flowing through Azure marketplace)?
- Any operational changes on our side (entitlement sync, SKUs)?

We're aiming for the change to happen before our renewal on 2027-03-01, but we need to understand if that's realistic. Happy to schedule a 30-min call this week.

Thanks,
Sara Lim
Procurement Manager, SlateBridge
[sara.mobile: +1 415-555-0199]

[Attachment: SB-MAP-request.xlsx (spreadsheet, 18KB)]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <procurement@slatebridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SlateBridge billing migration to Azure Marketplace — impact & timelines

Hi Sara — great to meet you over email. Thanks for the clear list of questions. High level answers below and I've attached a short worksheet and our mutual action plan (MAP) draft to make next steps concrete.

Short answers:
- Economics: Marketplace list pricing is generally the same but unit economics shift because of marketplace fees and potential reseller margins; for SlateBridge we estimate the effective price will be ~2.5% higher unless we apply an equivalent marketplace-enabled discount.
- Existing commitments: We can preserve committed discounts via an amendment. That typically requires a short-term amendment to map your current committed spend to marketplace SKUs; our sales/legal teams can draft this.
- Cutover timing: Operational cutover to start invoice issuance through Azure Marketplace typically takes 4–6 weeks once paperwork is signed and entitlements are reconciled. If we start the MAP this week, March 1st is tight but possible with parallel work.
- Operational changes: You'll need an entitlement sync (we provide a one-time script), and someone on your side to confirm Azure subscription linkage. No code changes required.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Review the attached pricing worksheet and MAP (attached).
2) 30-minute call with finance + procurement this week to agree discount preservation and target cutover date — are you available Thurs 1/14 or Fri 1/15?
3) If agreed, we will produce an amendment and a DocuSign link for signatures, and our ops team will schedule the entitlement sync.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx, SB-MAP-v2.pdf

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0123

Kimberly / Marissa — looping in for commercial alignment. A couple of notes from the renewals desk:

- If we need to preserve the current committed discount, the cleanest path is a short amendment that binds the commitment to the marketplace SKU with a credit clause for any overlap. Legal can do a lightweight redline.
- For a mid-term channel shift, we usually offer a marketplace-enabled credit to make the effective rate neutral for the customer for the first billing cycle. For SlateBridge's size I'd propose a 2.5% marketplace credit for the first 3 months (can be in the amendment).
- Need confirmation on whether SlateBridge requires invoicing to a different legal entity on Azure — that changes billing ops.

Marissa — can you prepare a one-page CFO-ready summary that shows: current ARR, proposed marketplace ARR, the proposed credit, and the DocuSign amendment? If you can have that by EOD Friday 1/15, I will route approvals.

Thanks,
Grace
